scope.transfer_note: WikiTable source/data rules can transfer across WTQ, SQA, TabFact, and wiki-like tables when table headers/cells expose matching surfaces. They do not encode SQA follow-up or TabFact verdict protocol.
scope.prompt_surface_note: Prompt text renders source/data rules only; task-protocol and output-contract rules live in separate feature families.

paper_dataset_characteristics: WTQ uses semi-structured Wikipedia tables; local overview records it as the flat WikiTable anchor benchmark.
SQA is derived from WTQ questions/tables but adds sequential interaction outside the dataset-domain feature.
TabFact uses Wikipedia tables for table-grounded fact verification; dataset-domain rules should remain table-source rules, not verdict protocol.

Source split and semantic matrix artifacts identify recurring WikiTable surfaces: country/code aliases, identifiers, atomic scores/dates/seasons, adjacent role groups, row order, and ordinal-vs-magnitude columns.
failure_patterns: Country or chart abbreviations are returned as raw codes or expanded in the wrong role.
Score/date/season/code cells are split or partially copied when they should remain atomic.
Models choose identifiers, ranks, or neighboring metrics instead of the requested entity/value role.
Repeated metric columns get attached to the wrong adjacent team/candidate/entity group.

payload.content:
Use these WikiTable source rules when relevant:
- Treat compact all-caps values in country, nationality, represent, team, city, or location columns as possible country/team abbreviations. Keep the code itself when the question asks for a code.
- In music chart tables, country-code headers such as GER, UK, or US name chart columns. Select the requested chart column rather than returning the header code as an entity.
- Treat score strings such as 18-12, 58-13, or 14-14 as complete result cells for lookup or evidence checks. Split them only when the question or statement asks for margin, difference, winner side, or loser side.
- Decide whether the target column is ordinal or magnitude before comparing. Rank, place, seed, pick, and chart position usually use lower-is-better; points, votes, sales, attendance, and medals usually use larger-is-more.
- If the requested value is a name, title, place, or entity, return the named entity column rather than an identifier, code, rank, glyph, or neighboring metric. Return the identifier only when that field is explicitly requested.
- Interpret first, last, previous, next, before, after, and directly after by displayed row order unless the prompt explicitly asks to sort by a column value.
- Bind repeated metric columns to the nearest entity or parent header before selecting or computing. Scores, votes, percentages, and populations usually belong to the adjacent team, candidate, country, or city group.
- Preserve atomic formatted values such as dates, seasons, scores, route codes, glyph identifiers, production codes, and episode numbers unless the prompt asks to transform or compute over them.

Apply these source rules only when the table surface matches. If a rule conflicts with explicit prompt wording or table evidence, follow the explicit wording and evidence. Do not change the required output format.

rationale: Dataset-domain/source-surface rule bundle grounded in dataset characteristics and observed failure patterns. It intentionally excludes task protocol and output contract behavior.
